claim.pdf_says: Term / Subclause table with two rows: "constant-entry 13.9, Constant entry" and "record-description-entry 13.10, Record description entry"
claim.markdown_says:
| constant-entry | 13.9, Constant entry |

record-description-entry 13.10, Record description entry
claim.why_it_matters: The last row of the meta-language term table (13.3.1) fell out of the markdown table and became a loose paragraph, so a table reader sees only constant-entry mapped to its subclause. The text is present; the table structure is lost.

verdict.reasoning: The claim describes the two sources accurately. Printed page 233 (PDF p255) shows a plain two-column Term/Subclause list with two rows. The markdown has the first row as a pipe-table row and the second row ('record-description-entry 13.10, Record description entry') as a loose paragraph right after it. Every word of the second row is present, in order, next to the table, and it still pairs the term with 13.10. Nothing is missing, misquoted or changed in meaning. The difference is only markdown table formatting, which the verification criteria say to reject (formatting; does not change meaning). The general format above it (brackets around the file-description-entry alternatives, braces around the sort-merge alternatives, ellipses) is not part of this claim. A cosmetic fix that puts the row back in the table is still worth making.
